To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have proposed a maximum-likelihood estimation method for computing the average VLSI power consumption that can handle data having a mixture-density with an arbitrary (but a finite) number of component densities.
the proposed method can be used to accurately estimate the average power of a VLSI design and it can be used to identify the components of the power distribution of the circuit.

the maximum-likelihood estimation method can handle data with multiple components and that the expectation-maximization algorithm is an efficient computational procedure for estimating the parameters of the components.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a new maximum likelihood method for estimating the average power consumption.
the estimation of average power consumption of digital circuits.
the estimation of the power consumption of VSLI circuits from the power data obtained from simulation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method provides a more accurate and efficient way to compute the average power consumption for VLSI circuits.
the maximum-likelihood estimation is a very powerful tool in estimating the average power consumption.
the proposed algorithm can provide an accurate estimate of the power consumption of a VLSI circuit with a very small number of samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the maximum-likelihood estimation method provides a powerful tool for estimating the average power consumption in a VLSI chip.
the method is a practical and powerful alternative to Monte Carlo estimation for estimating the power distribution of VLSI designs.
we have developed an algorithm to estimate the average power consumption from simulated power data that has a multi-component probability distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the maximum-likelihood estimation method can provide more accurate power estimation results compared to Monte Carlo and other existing methods.
a maximum-likelihood estimate can be obtained for a mixture distribution by an iterative procedure.
the EM algorithm can be applied to power estimation problems and it is more accurate and faster than the Monte Carlo method.
